translationRepairs: When Cao Cao took Hanzhong, Li Te's grandfather brought five hundred-odd households over to serve him; Cao enfeoffed him as a general and resettled the clan in Lüeyang, where northerners again labelled them Ba Di.

When Cao Cao took Hanzhong, Li Te's grandfather brought five hundred-odd households over to serve him; Cao appointed him as a general and resettled the clan in Lüeyang, where northerners again labelled them Ba Di.
拜為將軍 is an appointment to general, not a grant of a fief; replacing 'enfeoffed' with 'appointed' restores that meaning without other change.
Lord Lin replied: "I must win you fertile fields worthy of a lord; I cannot linger here."
Lord Lin replied: "I must seek lands for my lordship; I cannot linger here."

為君求廩地 is Lord Lin seeking 廩 territory in order to rule, not winning fields for the salt goddess; the proposed 'granary lands to rule' is stiff, so the sentence is recast while keeping the original's 'linger'.

Li Te's brother Li Xiang led his kinsmen, brothers-in-law Li Han and Ren Hui, Shangguan Dun, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Tuo of Shiping, the Di leaders Fu Cheng and Wei Bo, and four thousand horsemen to Zhao Xin's banner.

Li Te's younger brother Li Xiang led his brothers and his sister's husband Li Han, together with Ren Hui, Shangguan Dun, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Tuo of Shiping, the Di leaders Fu Cheng and Wei Bo, and others, with four thousand horsemen, to Zhao Xin's banner.
弟 marks Xiang as younger brother; 妹夫 governs 李含 only, so 任回 is a following name, not a second brother-in-law; 兄弟 and 等 are also restored.
Zhao Xin composed himself and answered: "You speak my mind exactly—you are the merchants who woke Confucius to wisdom; heaven sends you to finish what I began."
Zhao Xin composed himself and answered: "Your words hit my intent exactly—one may say, as in the line 'it is Shang who brings me insight'; heaven has sent you to complete my affair."
起予者商 is the Analects line about the disciple Shang, not merchants and not an explicit naming of Confucius.
Seize the mandate of the hour, follow men's hearts, lift the people from ruin, and show all creation where loyalty lies—the empire will settle, far beyond Ba and Shu alone."
It is fitting to answer the season of Heaven, follow men's hearts, lift the people from ruin, and show all creation where loyalty lies—then the realm can be settled, and not Yong and Shu alone."
庸、蜀 is Yong and Shu, not Ba and Shu, and 宜應天時 is hortatory ('it is fitting to answer Heaven's season'), not the imperative 'Seize'.

Before this, Huidi took Liang provincial inspector Luo Shang as Pacify-West general, concurrently Protect Western Yi colonel, Yi provincial inspector; supervised gate general Wang Dun, Shangfang commandant Yi Xin, Shu commandery prefect Xu Jian, Guanghan prefect Xin Ran etc. altogether seven thousand-odd men enter Shu.

Before this, Huidi took Liang provincial inspector Luo Shang as Pacify-West general, concurrently Protect Western Yi colonel, Yi provincial inspector; supervised gate general Wang Dun, Shangyong commandant Yi Xin, Shu commandery prefect Xu Jian, Guanghan prefect Xin Ran etc. altogether seven thousand-odd men enter Shu.
上庸 is Shangyong; Shangfang is a false reading confined to the literal English.
When Li Te learned Luo Shang was coming he sent his brother Li Xiang ahead with rich gifts to greet him.
When Li Te learned Luo Shang was coming he was greatly afraid and sent his younger brother Li Xiang ahead on the road with tribute treasures to greet him.
The envoy is 弟驤, a younger brother distinct from executed 庠, and the original omits 甚懼 and flattens 于道奉迎，並貢寶物.
Shi having arrived; saw Ran camp palisades choke points; plotted surprise drifting people; sighed saying: Without bandits yet wall—enemy surely guards there.
Shi having arrived, saw Ran palisading choke points and plotting to ambush the drifting people, and sighed saying: Without bandits yet they wall—the enemy will surely occupy them.

見冉營柵沖要，謀掩流人 makes Xin Ran the one palisading and plotting the ambush, so Yan Shi must not be the subject of 謀; but 仇必保焉 means the enemy will occupy those works, not that a slaughter is being prepared.
Luo Shang told his officers: "Those rebels were ripe for removal, yet Guanghan ignored my counsel and swelled the enemy's strength—what are we to do now?"
Luo Shang told his officers: "These rebels have already succeeded in getting away, yet Guanghan ignored my counsel and swelled the enemy's strength—what are we to do now?"
此虜成去矣 means the rebels have already succeeded in getting away, not that they were ripe for removal.

Li Fu became general of agile cavalry, Li Xiang general of swift cavalry, eldest son Li Shi general of martial awe, Li Dang general who garrisons the army, youngest Li Xiong vanguard general; Li Han served as colonel of the Western Yi while Guoli, Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, and Fei Tuo led divisions; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, and Qu Xin formed his striking force; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, and Wang Huai staffed headquarters; Yan Shi directed strategy with He Shi and Zhao Su as his closest confidants.

Elder brother Li Fu became general of agile cavalry, younger brother Li Xiang general of fierce cavalry, eldest son Li Shi general of martial awe, second son Li Dang general who garrisons the army, youngest son Li Xiong vanguard general; Li Han served as colonel of the Western Yi while Han's sons Li Guo and Li Li, together with Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, and Fei Tuo, led divisions; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, and Qu Xin formed his striking force; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, and Wang Huai staffed headquarters; Yan Shi directed strategy with He Shi and Zhao Su as his closest confidants.
含子國離 is two sons, Guo and Li, as later 含子離 confirms; 兄/弟/次子 were dropped; 驍騎 should be distinguished from 驃騎. The proposal's wholesale restyling of titles and dropping of surnames is unnecessary.
In the first year of Taian Li Te styled himself governor of Yi Province, commander over Liang and Yi, grand general and commander-in-chief, adopted the reign title Jianchu, and proclaimed an amnesty.

In the first year of Taian, Li Te styled himself governor of Yi Province, commander over Liang and Yi, grand general and commander-in-chief, adopted the reign title Jianchu, and proclaimed an amnesty.
A comma after the year phrase keeps 太安元年 from attaching to Li Te as a fused personal name.

During the campaign against Zhang Zheng, Li Te stationed Li Xiang with Li Pan, Ren Hui, and Li Gong at Pi Bridge to watch Luo Shang.
Without the comma, 'Zhang Zheng Li Te' can be read as one name; the pause after 張征 matches the Chinese.
After taking refuge in Yi Province Inspector Zhao Xin singled him out for favour.
After taking refuge in Yi Province, Inspector Zhao Xin singled him out for favour.
The comma after Yi Province keeps 刺史 as Zhao Xin's office, not a fused locative-title string.

Li Han's son Li Li galloped from Zitong when he heard his father meant to yield—too late to dissuade him—so he fell back with Li Xiong to plot a night attack on Sun Fu, proposing: "If we prevail, we shall rotate supreme command between us every three years."

Li Han's son Li Li galloped from Zitong when he heard his father meant to yield—too late to dissuade him—so he fell back with Li Xiong to plot a raid on Sun Fu, proposing: "If we prevail, we shall rotate supreme command between us every three years."
襲阜軍 is a raid on Sun Fu's army and does not specify a night attack.

As Li Liu lay dying he told his commanders: "General of nimble cavalry Li Xiong is humane and keen—his counsel is inspired—enough to finish our task; yet the vanguard's martial dash seems heaven-sent. Accept joint direction under the forward commander and raise Li Xiong as Prince of Chengdu."

As Li Liu lay dying he told his commanders: "The General of Nimble Cavalry is humane and keen—his counsel is inspired—enough to finish our task; yet the vanguard commander is heroic and martial, almost heaven-aided. Accept joint direction under the forward commander and make him Prince of Chengdu."
驍騎 and 前軍 are two offices; the original wrongly names both as Li Xiong, whereas 以為成都王 refers to the forward commander.
He died the same year at fifty-six.
時年五十六 is his age at death; 時年 is not 'the same year'.

unresolvedReferences.description: Emperor Hui (惠帝) frames Luo Shang's appointment, but the packet supplies no reign-year mapping to a Western date.
The seventh-month refugee deadline has no accompanying reign or calendar year.
Analects figure 商 is named only in Zhao Xin's quotation; no independent activity date is given.
Cheng Tang and King Wu appear only as Tang-Wu exemplars in Li Xiang's speech.
含子國離 may name two sons of Li Han (Guo and Li) rather than one person Guoli; packet English treats one name, which this extraction follows.
The 驍騎 title in Li Liu's dying speech may name a second commander besides 前軍 / Li Xiong; the owned unit never identifies that officer.
元康四年 names an era-year for Li Xiang's xiaolian nomination without a packet reign mapping, so the Western year remains a research hold.
